propositions: Two concurrent reducer cache writers (write_cache and corrupt-CREATE handler in _processors.py) share a fixed .cache.json.tmp artifact, allowing overlapping file descriptors to mutate the file after one writer renames it into place as .cache.json, violating atomic publication

A reducer can observe different event generations concurrently; one writer's rename can expose a partially-written inode while another writer continues mutating it, splicing fields from independent generations and creating a cache with current-hash but stale state
Cache invalidation and deterministic replay contracts are violated when a subsequent reduction returns stale cached state instead of detecting the incoherent envelope or replaying from events

The repair consolidates all cache writers (write_cache and process_create) through a canonical atomic_write mechanism with unique per-directory temps and atomic replace, ensuring coherent envelope publication under concurrency
